This page lists **all 184 tools** registered on aihydro-tools `v2.12.0`, exactly as the agent sees them. Tools are grouped by **tier** (how readily they are surfaced to the agent) and **domain**.

### Meteorological Forcing

#### `compute_drought_index` · :material-fire: hot

Compute a standardised drought index (SPI or SPEI) from forcing data in the session. Aggregates daily precip (and PET for SPEI) to monthly, accumulates over the scale window, and standardises per calendar month to a unit-normal scale (negative = drier than normal). Writes session.drought. Requires fetch_forcing_data first (with PET for SPEI).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `session_id` | any | — |  |
| `index` | string | — |  |
| `scale_months` | integer | — |  |
| `min_month_fraction` | any | — |  |

```python
compute_drought_index(session_id='01646500', index='spi')
```

#### `train_hydro_model` · :material-fire: hot

Kick off a model training job (detached subprocess). Returns {job_id} immediately — poll with get_training_status (≤1× per minute). Requires watershed+forcing+streamflow (unless streamflow_source='camels'). framework: hbv (HBV-light, default). Neural backends are unavailable pending verification. epochs / learning_rate / n_restarts / hidden_size: leave unset for the backend's own defaults (HBV 500 epochs, lr 0.05; neural 30 epochs, lr 0.001). streamflow_source: where the observed discharge comes from, recorded in the result. "session" (default) = the flow already fetched into the study (fetch_streamflow_data); no network call is made and missing flow is an error (MISSING_STREAMFLOW / MISSING_PREREQUISITES). "camels" = explicit opt-in to the CAMELS-US benchmark record downloaded via pygeohydro (a gauge outside CAMELS is an error, never a silent fallback to session flow). The request goes through the same gate as propose_and_train: periods must be disjoint (train &lt; val &lt; test), values in range, and the backend available. Typical runtime: 2-15 min (HBV).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `session_id` | any | — |  |
| `workspace_dir` | any | — |  |
| `framework` | string | — |  |
| `model` | string | — |  |
| `train_start` | string | — |  |
| `train_end` | string | — |  |
| `val_start` | string | — |  |
| `val_end` | string | — |  |
| `test_start` | string | — |  |
| `test_end` | string | — |  |
| `epochs` | any | — |  |
| `n_restarts` | any | — |  |
| `hidden_size` | any | — |  |
| `learning_rate` | any | — |  |
| `streamflow_source` | string | — |  |

```python
train_hydro_model(session_id='01646500', workspace_dir='...')
```

### Streamflow

#### `compute_flood_frequency` · :material-fire: hot

Estimate design floods (return periods) from streamflow in the session via flood frequency analysis. Extracts annual maxima, fits a distribution, and returns return levels for 2–500 yr with bootstrap confidence intervals. Writes session.flood_frequency. Requires fetch_streamflow_data first and ≥10 years of daily data for a meaningful fit.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `session_id` | any | — |  |
| `distribution` | string | — |  |
| `method` | string | — |  |
| `year_type` | string | — |  |
| `min_year_fraction` | any | — |  |
| `year_start_month` | any | — |  |

```python
compute_flood_frequency(session_id='01646500', distribution='gumbel')
```

#### `extract_hydrological_signatures` · :material-fire: hot

Extract 17 CAMELS-style hydrological signatures (flow stats, BFI, runoff ratio, elasticity, high/low flow events, FDC slope, timing). `q5` / `q95` are the 5% / 95% flow quantiles (low / high flow, CAMELS), not exceedance flows; `flow_quantile_convention` marks results that follow this. Requires delineate_watershed first. Defaults to CAMELS analysis period 1989-10-01 to 2009-09-30.

#### `compute_soil_loss_rusle` · :material-fire: hot

Estimate basin-average annual soil loss with RUSLE (A = R·K·LS·C·P, t·ha⁻¹·yr⁻¹). Each factor is taken from an explicit argument if given, otherwise derived from session forcing (R), soil (K: SSURGO recorded Kw from fetch_soil_attributes_ssurgo if present, else EPIC from texture), geomorphic slope (LS), and land cover (C) using standard documented formulas. Writes session.soil_loss.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `session_id` | any | — |  |
| `r_factor` | any | — |  |
| `k_factor` | any | — |  |

#### `compute_twi` · :material-fire: hot

### CAMELS Attributes

#### `fetch_camels_us` · :material-fire: hot

CAMELS-US static catchment attributes (671 minimally-disturbed CONUS gauges). Single gauge via ``gauge_id`` (cached in session) OR bulk via ``gauge_ids`` (list, [] = all 671; saved to workspace). Returns ~60 attributes in the flat ``attributes`` dict, plus ``attribute_group_index`` (topography/climate/hydrology/soil/vegetation/ geology -&gt; attribute names). Citation: Addor et al. (2017), HESS 21. session_id : str | None (optional from Wave 3) — auto-resolved from chat context.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `session_id` | any | — |  |
| `gauge_id` | any | — |  |
| `gauge_ids` | any | — |  |

```python
fetch_camels_us(session_id='01646500', gauge_id='01646500')
```

### Citations & Literature

#### `get_citation_by_doi`

Resolve a citation by exact DOI (uses cache when fresh). Same schema as lookup_citation. The DOI endpoint is used, never a search, and the DOI the provider returns must equal the one asked for. Network failure is `unavailable`, not `not_found`. A string that is not a DOI is refused.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `doi` | string | yes |  |
| `force_refresh` | boolean | — |  |

```python
get_citation_by_doi(doi='...')
```

#### `index_literature`

Scan a folder of papers (.txt, .md, .pdf via pypdf) and build a text-only searchable index (literature_index.md with first ~800 chars per doc). Re-run when papers are added. folder_path defaults to ~/.aihydro/projects/&lt;name&gt;/literature/.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `project_name` | string | yes |  |
| `folder_path` | any | — |  |

```python
index_literature(project_name='...')
```

#### `lookup_citation`

Look up a citation (free text or DOI). Cascade: CrossRef → Semantic Scholar → DataCite. Cached at ~/.aihydro/citations/ (30 day TTL).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `query` | string | yes |  |
| `source_hint` | any | — |  |
| `force_refresh` | boolean | — |  |

```python
lookup_citation(query='...')
```

#### `search_literature`

Query the literature index. Text match on filenames + excerpts, no vector DB. return_full_content=True returns full text of matched docs for the LLM to synthesise (can be large).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `project_name` | string | yes |  |
| `query` | string | yes |  |
| `return_full_content` | boolean | — |  |

```python
search_literature(project_name='...', query='...')
```

#### `list_available_tools` · :material-fire: hot

Browse the registered MCP tools (built-in + community plugins). Each answer is capped at about 4k characters and sorted by name. No arguments: names with a one-line summary, one page at a time (follow next_offset). domain=&lt;name&gt;: only that domain's tools (see aihydro_describe_capability for the domains). name=&lt;tool&gt;: that one tool in full. offset below 0 is treated as 0; limit of 0, None or below 1 means no limit beyond the size cap. For parameters of a tool you are about to call, describe_tool(name) is the usual call.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `domain` | any | — |  |

| `limit` | any | — |  |

#### `ensure_project`

Host operation. Return the project of a workspace directory, creating it when there is none (the backend mints the `prj_<ULID>` id). Idempotent. A new project is filled with the studies whose workspace_dir is this folder; its default study is only a suggestion until a person confirms it. attach_to: an existing project id that moved here; its old folder is kept as a root_dir_alias.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `root_dir` | string | yes |  |
| `attach_to` | any | — |  |

```python
ensure_project(root_dir='...')
```

Host operation. Unlink a study from a project. The study, its run log and claims are untouched; if it was the default, the default (and its confirmation) is cleared.

| `project_id` | string | yes |  |
| `study_id` | string | yes |  |
| `expected_revision` | any | — |  |

```python

```

Host operation. Set a project's title (locks it: title_source becomes "user"). expected_revision: the revision last read; a REVISION_CONFLICT error means another writer changed the project first.

| `expected_revision` | any | — |  |

#### `archive_session`

Freeze the session: its interpretation and notes are marked historical in the study context. Use when concluding a study phase. Archived sessions stay readable and exportable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `session_id` | any | — |  |

```python
archive_session(session_id='01646500')
```

#### `clear_session`

Clear cached results to force recompute. Notes/workspace_dir/site_name/ interpretation are always preserved. slots: subset of [watershed, streamflow, signatures, geomorphic, camels, forcing, twi, cn, model] (omit for all data slots).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `session_id` | any | — |  |
| `slots` | any | — |  |

```python
clear_session(session_id='01646500', slots='...')
```

#### `get_session_health`

Audit a session for identity drift, workspace problems, and consistency gaps. Returns warnings keyed by code so the agent can fix issues before they propagate into exports, or downstream tools.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `session_id` | any | — |  |

```python
get_session_health(session_id='01646500')
```

#### `get_session_raw_state`

Phase 1 of interpretation: return raw computed state for the LLM to read (large arrays summarised). Follow with write_research_interpretation to author + persist the prose synthesis.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `session_id` | any | — |  |

```python
get_session_raw_state(session_id='01646500')
```

#### `get_session_summary` · :material-fire: hot

Return computed/pending slots for the session + notes + interpretation. session_id is optional — auto-resolved from the active chat when omitted.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `session_id` | any | — |  |

```python
get_session_summary(session_id='01646500')
```

#### `merge_session_shards`

Consolidate sub-agent shard files into the main session (notes, citations, slots). Shard files are deleted after merge. shard_ids: subset or omit to merge all available shards.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `session_id` | any | — |  |
| `shard_ids` | any | — |  |

```python
merge_session_shards(session_id='01646500', shard_ids='...')
```

#### `start_session` · :material-fire: hot

Start or resume a research session (persistent memory for a study). session_id: any string (slug, USGS gauge id, UUID); auto-generated if omitted. With a session_id, the current chat is bound to that study. workspace_dir: pass once, remembered for all future calls — enables auto-save of tool outputs there. shard_id: for sub-agent forks. include_packages: also return `available_packages` ({name: version} of the MCP interpreter; ~12k characters and a slow `pip list`, so off by default). Only the last 5 notes are returned (`notes_total` counts all; get_session_summary has them all).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `session_id` | any | — |  |
| `shard_id` | any | — |  |
| `workspace_dir` | any | — |  |
| `include_packages` | boolean | — |  |

```python
start_session(session_id='01646500', shard_id='...')
```

|-----------|------|----------|-------------|

Load a skill's full SKILL.md (frontmatter + body). The skill's steps and format contracts are binding — see SKILL DISCOVERY in the system prompt. name: exact match from list_skills().

| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `workspace_dir` | any | — |  |

```python
load_skill(name='...')
```

#### `save_skill`

Persist a new SKILL.md (Agent Skills open format) to ~/.aihydro/skills/agent-created/. Use after completing a novel workflow worth reusing. name will be slugified; content is the markdown body.

| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `description` | string | yes |  |
| `content` | string | yes |  |
| `domain` | string | — |  |
| `when_to_use` | string | — |  |
| `tags` | any | — |  |
| `tools_used` | any | — |  |

```python
save_skill(name='...', description='...', content='...')
```
